hunt.justification: AI-assisted BEC represents a material financial risk, as traditional phishing filters may miss the high-fidelity lures. This hunt provides assurance that the organizational accounting/finance departments have not been compromised by this specific $50,000 ACH campaign.

meta.name: AI-Assisted Executive Impersonation and Invoice Fraud

related.reason: Executive impersonation often follows credential or session theft; this hunt should be paired with a search for anomalous executive logons.

meta.analysis: A standard detection rule might flag the static domains, but this hunt baselines all 'ServiceNow' variants and looks for the rare creation of PDF invoices across multiple surfaces, allowing it to catch infrastructure shifts that AI-assisted actors frequently deploy.

coverage.reason: Attribution of multi-hop proxy chains (T1090.003) is not possible with the available endpoint or network connection surfaces.

stages.name: AI-Assisted Phishing and Lure Interaction
observables: AI markers: HTML comments, em-dash symbols '—', banner lines '==========='
CEO/CFO impersonation in sender and reply-to display names
Bank transfer instructions for ACH payments of nearly $50,000

stages.name: Multi-hop Traffic Obfuscation
observables: Traffic to impersonation domains via multi-hop proxies or ORB networks

scenario.summary: An AI-assisted business email compromise (BEC) campaign targeted finance teams with ACH payment fraud by impersonating executives and vendors like ServiceNow. The attackers used generative AI to create highly uniform templates, fabricated email threads, and itemized invoices, delivering them through lookalike domains and third-party email infrastructure.

meta.rationale: Start by identifying hosts with ServiceNow packages to find likely finance/admin targets; then expand to the whole estate via DNS if those hosts are clean.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker is using lookalike domains and AI-generated invoice lures to trick finance personnel into processing fraudulent ACH payments, following a pattern of impersonating executives and vendors like ServiceNow.

scope_hosts.description: Hosts to narrow the search; leave empty to hunt across the estate.

impersonation_domains.description: Lookalike domains used for phishing and reply-to infrastructure.

references.name: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud

blind_spots.risk: Attackers using multi-hop proxies (T1090.003) might appear as internal traffic or generic browser traffic, masking the adversary origin.
blind_spots.question: Was the connection to the lookalike domain made via an ORB proxy network?
blind_spots.requires: Forward proxy or full HTTP inspection with user-agent logging
blind_spots.remediation: Ensure hb_http_activity includes user_agent and authenticated user info.

blind_spots.risk: We are hunting for the aftermath (DNS/Files) rather than the delivery; if the user deletes the email without downloading the invoice, we may miss the targeting.
blind_spots.question: Did the email contain the specific AI-assisted markers (em-dash, custom banners)?
blind_spots.requires: hb_email_activity or direct M365 audit logs
blind_spots.remediation: Onboard hb_email_activity to enable keyword searches in subjects and bodies.

hunt.name: AI-Assisted Executive Impersonation and Invoice Fraud
hunt.description: This hunt identifies internal hosts interacting with lookalike infrastructure (e.g., service-nowinc.com) and the subsequent creation of fraudulent invoice PDF artifacts. It leverages the correlation between DNS resolutions, rare HTTP traffic to non-standard vendor domains, and file creation events in user-writable paths to isolate victims of high-fidelity Business Email Compromise (BEC).

nodes.label: Scope by ServiceNow software or connectors

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%servicenow%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%servicenow%'
config.description: Identify hosts that have ServiceNow software or related connectors installed, representing likely targets or relevant business units.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames belonging to users or departments that interact with ServiceNow.

primitive_config.label: Scope by ServiceNow software or connectors
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%servicenow%' OR LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%servicenow%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames belonging to users or departments that interact with ServiceNow.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) AS lookups, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{impersonation_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
config.description: Find any host resolving the specific impersonation domains identified in the research.
config.expected_signal: Hostnames resolving domains like service-nowinc.com; silence means no interaction with the known primary infrastructure.

primitive_config.label: DNS lookups to lookalike domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) AS lookups, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{impersonation_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
primitive_config.expected: Hostnames resolving domains like service-nowinc.com; silence means no interaction with the known primary infrastructure.

nodes.label: Rare HTTP variants of ServiceNow hostnames

config.content: SELECT url_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_http_activity WHERE url_hostname LIKE '%service-now%' AND url_hostname NOT LIKE '%.service-now.com' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY url_hostname HAVING host_count < 3
config.description: Baseline web traffic to variants of 'ServiceNow' to catch domains not named in the initial report but following the same pattern.
config.expected_signal: Hosts connecting to service-nowinc.com or other lookalikes that stand out from standard corporate traffic.

primitive_config.label: Rare HTTP variants of ServiceNow hostnames
primitive_config.content: SELECT url_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_http_activity WHERE url_hostname LIKE '%service-now%' AND url_hostname NOT LIKE '%.service-now.com' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY url_hostname HAVING host_count < 3
primitive_config.expected: Hosts connecting to service-nowinc.com or other lookalikes that stand out from standard corporate traffic.

nodes.label: ServiceNow PDF creation in user paths

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_name, file_path, process_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id = 1 AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.pdf%' AND LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%servicenow%' AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\downloads\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\desktop\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/downloads/%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify the creation of PDF files containing 'ServiceNow' in the filename, indicative of the fraudulent invoice being saved.
config.expected_signal: Creation of PDF invoices in user profiles on hosts previously identified as targets or interactors.

nodes.label: Coordinate with Finance and review communication

config.description: Final manual check to confirm if an ACH transfer was initiated and to look for AI markers in email.
config.instructions: Review the user's M365 mail flow for the subjects 'due bill' or 'ACH Parment'. Check for AI markers (em-dash, banner lines) in the message body. Contact Finance to ensure no ACH payments of ~$50,000 were processed for the impersonated vendors.
